baseline.description: No perception error, no fusion. Reference case every other scenario is compared against.

sensor_noise.description: Gaussian position noise on real detections only.

latency.description: Detections delayed before reaching the controller.

confidence_error.description: Reported detection confidence is miscalibrated (noisy) relative to true detection quality, with no fusion to compensate.

no_fusion_matched.description: Same error conditions as naive_fusion/trust_weighted_fusion (FN=0.2, noise=1.5, confidence_error=0.15) but with fusion disabled. Exists so fusion mode is the only variable that changes across the three fusion-comparison scenarios; do not compare naive_fusion/trust_weighted_fusion against confidence_error or baseline for that purpose, since those use different error profiles.

naive_fusion.description: Moderate noise + missed detections, combined across UAVs with unweighted (naive) averaging fusion.

trust_weighted_fusion.description: Same error conditions as naive_fusion, but fused using each UAV's confidence as a trust weight.

one_uav_obstacle.description: Task 7, scenario 1: a single static obstacle directly in the swarm's path - the baseline single-entity case every other multi-entity scenario below is a variation on.

multiple_obstacles.description: Task 7, scenario 2: three static obstacles strung along the swarm's diagonal route to the rally point, forcing repeated avoidance rather than a single one-off dodge.

two_crossing_targets.description: Task 7, scenario 3: two moving targets on paths that cross near the world center, patrolling back and forth (bounce) so the crossing recurs over the run instead of happening once.

moving_obstacle_approaching_swarm.description: Task 7, scenario 4: an obstacle starting well clear of the swarm's start cluster and moving steadily toward it, so the threat range/bearing genuinely closes over time instead of being static from step 0.

target_temporarily_lost.description: Task 7, scenario 5: a moving target that bounces back and forth vertically through x=50 (the middle of the swarm's diagonal route to the rally point), so it repeatedly sweeps into radar coverage as it crosses the corridor and back out of coverage as it moves toward y=0 or y=100 - genuinely leaving true sensor range for stretches of the run, not just suffering perception error.

target_reappearing_after_dropout.description: Task 7, scenario 6: a target that stays continuously within radar coverage, paired with periodic total sensor dropout - so it disappears and reappears in the detection stream purely due to the sensor blacking out, not because it ever actually left range.

clutter_near_real_target.description: Task 7, scenario 7: a real target sitting in the swarm's path with elevated radar clutter/false-alarm rates, so genuine detections and clutter false alarms both show up in the same radar coverage area - a harder discrimination case than clutter in empty space.

closely_spaced_targets.description: Task 7, scenario 8: two targets close enough together (8 units apart, inside sensor_range but outside safe formation spacing) to stress whether detections/tracks stay resolved as two distinct entities instead of blurring into one.
